summary: Consolidating the four questions to match the evidence that actually exists. The child premise question is marked explained: its control receipt shows the held-proposal effect requires the member to be dropped from both halves, and a member kept as an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left proposes in 0 ms and commits on all nodes. The recovery question is also marked explained: the restarted member recovered the entry committed while it was down, relearned the leader and proposed successfully, with its single-restart, no-snapshot scope recorded in the interpretation. The exploration question is deliberately left open, because the one combination it has not sampled is restarts of members inside the randomized run, which is worth one execution with member rebuilds from the persisted storage that the driver keeps up to date. The bookkeeping submission carries no new experiment and requests no execution; the summarized state of the audit is one asserted defect with eight witness receipts and four independent controls, two bounded safety negatives with explicit scope, one recovery scenario, and the remaining limitations recorded per question.
